## Summary

**`stream_channel.py` — `StreamChannel`**
- `_items` now stores `(stamp, item)` tuples (`deque[tuple[int, T]]`).
- Added `_mux` reference (default `None`) and a `_bind_mux(mux)` method to associate a channel with its owning mux.
- `push()` now assigns a stamp on **every** call: from `mux._next_push_seq()` when bound to a mux, or `0` when standalone. The stamp is drawn unconditionally (even when unsubscribed) so stamps stay unique/strictly increasing across all of a mux's channels — including `_events`.
- Both `_sync_cursor` and `_async_cursor` strip the stamp, yielding only raw items during normal iteration (`tee`/`atee` inherit this via `__iter__`).

**`_mux.py` — `StreamMux`**
- Added the shared `_push_seq` counter and `_next_push_seq()` (returns 1, 2, 3, … so mux stamps never collide with the standalone `0` sentinel).
- Bound the internal `_events` channel to the mux (`self._events._bind_mux(self)`) so forwarded protocol events consume stamps from the same counter.
- Bind every projection channel to the mux in `_bind_and_wire`.

**`run_stream.py` — `GraphRunStream.interleave`**
- Rewrote from round-robin to a **stamp-ordered merge**: always yields the buffered item with the lowest stamp (correct because stamps are globally monotonic, so a not-yet-produced item can only have a larger stamp). Drives the shared pump when no channel has a buffered item.
- Validation and subscription are now **eager** (at call time, not first iteration): unknown names raise `KeyError`; an already-subscribed channel raises `RuntimeError` containing `'already has a subscriber'`, releasing any channels subscribed so far first.
- A `finally` block releases all subscriptions (`_subscribed = False`) on normal completion, early close, or error. Channel errors (via `fail`) propagate to the caller; empty channels contribute nothing.

- Validated every spec bullet with standalone scripts: standalone stamp-0, mux monotonic stamps skipping `_events`-consumed values, arrival-order merge, empty-channel skip, early-close release, already-subscribed release-of-prior + `RuntimeError`, unknown-name `KeyError`, and error propagation after draining.
- The remaining failures in the existing test suite are all either (a) tests reading `_items` as raw items / expecting `interleave` to leave a subscription — both directly contradicting the new spec, so the verification patch updates them — or (b) pre-existing `GenericFakeChatModel.stream_v2` environment failures that I confirmed also fail on the clean tree.
